actionability.justification: The rule gives a concrete, checkable behavior change ('run its declared verification command... before' claiming completion) rather than a vague admonition to 'be careful,' though it leans on the assumption that a 'declared verification command' always exists to run.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: Broadening from 'release' to 'any fix, change, or validation/lint/test check' precisely matches the evidence span (ordinary fixes and lint/validation checks across 5 projects) without ballooning into an unfalsifiable platitude like 'always verify your work.'

leakage.justification: The remedy text and heading are fully generic ('any fix, change, or validation/lint/test check') with no mention of harbor, cinder, fake-aurora, or any other evidence-specific project noun.

routing_fitness.justification: Correctly picks the cheapest adequate fix — broadening an existing installed claude-md rule (R2) rather than minting a new skill (already covered in shape by R1) or an unworkable hook for a natural-language claim, with sound dedup verdicts across all six comparisons.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md standing rule rather than a skill, it has no discrete 'Use when ...' trigger; the applicability is only implicitly bounded by the heading and prose ('before reporting... complete or passing'), which is serviceable but not a crisp routing trigger.
